title: Why church music makes him despondent and the blues does not
summary: He can play the blues all day but church pieces from his upbringing make him despondent, so he avoids them in nightclubs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: It was kind of a Blues thing, you know. I guess people have always had Blues singers... I don't know. I guess every people that's oppressed and... Way deep in their mind, they have a Blues or a Church piece they think of. And all Church pieces give me the blues. They do. I don't know, but they make me feel sorta bluish. I don't know what it is. It's this heartstring pulling thing. That's why I don't like to play Church numbers in a Jazz spot, because I get despondent. Do you understand?

I can play the Blues. I don't get despondent with the Blues. But with Church music I get very despondent. You know? I just don't... There's a thing about that. I get... Well, I was raised, and people used to play these pieces and sing these numbers, you know. It makes me think about them so much, you know. And I don't like to get that way when I'm in a nightclub, playing -- you know?
I don't know what it is.
Well, the Blues expresses a different kind of feeling(?)...
The Blues is a different thing to me... I can play the Blues all day long. The Blues... A lot of is

like you're jammin', you know. But if you're playing a Church number that I've been raised on all the time for Church especially, that's when I really get the blues. I get very despondent. You know what I mean? So that's my ...(?). . .(?). . .
